item.title: Current Events - September 30, 2026
item.description:
September 30, 2026 (2026-09-30) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Iraqi conflict
    • Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
      • American troops complete their withdrawal from Iraq, ending their 23-year presence in the country that started with the 2003 U.S. invasion, and also the 12-year U.S. intervention against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria. (AP) (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
    • A United States federal judge approves media conglomerate Paramount Skydance's settlement with 12 states that challenged its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on antitrust grounds, allowing the $81 billion merger to proceed toward completion. (AFP via ABS-CBN News)

Disasters and accidents

  • A helicopter crashes in Marondera, Zimbabwe, killing all six people on board, including businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife. (AFP via Daily Sun) (The Citizen)
  • Seven workers are killed in a gas incident inside a mining tunnel in Itogon, Benguet, Philippines. (Manila Bulletin)

Law and crime

  • Capital punishment in the United States
    • Capital punishment in Tennessee
      • The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit halts Christa Pike's execution in Tennessee shortly before it was scheduled, to allow for further review of whether evidence of childhood sexual abuse was adequately considered at sentencing; the U.S. Supreme Court shortly after lifts the Sixth Circuit's stay order, allowing the execution to proceed. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
      • Pike is sent to a hospital following the failed administration of two rounds of the drugs used to perform the lethal injection. (Axios) (BBC News)
  • 2026 Turkish LGBTQ raids, Censorship in Turkey, Censorship of LGBTQ issues
    • A Turkish court orders the closure of independent news website T24 and its social media accounts after the justice ministry reported that T24 had published 118 items during the previous year which the court classified as "LGBTQ propaganda". (AFP via RTL Today)
  • Flydubai Flight 1073
    • A Flydubai flight from Dubai, United Arab Emirates, to Tel Aviv, Israel, is landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, by a relief crew after the copilot violently attacked the captain in an attempted aircraft hijacking. (BBC News) (CNN)
  • Narcotics in Bolivia
    • Bolivian police arrest attorney general Roger Mariaca and Santa Cruz de la Sierra prosecutor Alberto Zeballos after the U.S. State Department accused them of corruption and links to drug trafficking. Police also raid prosecutors' offices in several cities. (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Romanian political crisis
    • Romania's parliament rejects prime minister-designate Siegfried Mureșan's proposed government, receiving 182 of the 233 votes required for approval, prolonging the political crisis that began after Ilie Bolojan's government fell in May. (AFP) (AP)
  • At least 450 people are arrested and 76 people are injured after students in France protest over class overcrowding and teacher shortages. (BBC News) (The New York Times)

Science and technology

  • AI boom
    • The Tokyo District Court rules that a person's voice can receive protection under publicity rights, in Japan's first case involving alleged audio deepfake, while dismissing actor Kenjiro Tsuda's request to remove already-deleted TikTok videos. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - September 23, 2026
item.description:
September 23, 2026 (2026-09-23) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
      • 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
        • The United States Central Command says that the U.S. military has redirected 115 commercial vessels since the reinstatement of its blockade on July 14. (Gulf News)
      • An Indian wiper is killed during an attack on the bulk carrier MV Cape Dao near the Strait of Hormuz, with Oman's navy confirming that 27 crew members have been evacuated. (AFP and Reuters via Arab News) (The Indian Express)
    • Iran reopens schools and universities after months of closures caused by the war. About 16.5 million schoolchildren begin the new academic year, with reopening ceremonies held across the country. (AFP via Channels Television)
    • Acting United States Navy secretary Hung Cao reports that eight sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have attempted suicide during its long deployment including during the Iran war. (BBC News)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) seizes several airports in Tigray, while clashes are ongoing in the nearby regions of Afar and Amhara. The TPLF says that it has started a "defensive war" against the federal government of Ethiopia. (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Kharkiv strikes, Kyiv strikes, Odesa strikes
      • Russian drone and missile attacks across Ukraine kill at least eight civilians, including six agricultural workers in Kharkiv Oblast and two people in Kyiv, while strikes also hit Odesa. Ukraine says it intercepts or suppresses 119 of 161 drones. (AP)
    • Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Poland deploys fighter jets into its airspace after a Russian helicopter intruded near Braniewo, Warmian–Masurian Voivodeship. (Chronicle Live)
  • Colombian conflict
    • Threats and attacks by the Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada (ACSN) bring Santa Marta, Magdalena Department, Colombia, to a standstill, closing businesses and public transport. The group orders the shutdown after security forces kill 13 ACSN members. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
  • Communal conflicts in Nigeria
    • Fifteen people, including a village head, are killed in an armed ethnic clash in Bagudo, Kebbi State, Nigeria. Six suspects are arrested following the attack. (Daily Post)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war, United States sanctions against Iran
    • Iranian airlines suspend services to Azerbaijan, Baghdad, Georgia, Muscat, and Qatar, after new U.S. sanctions target Iran's aviation sector. (AFP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Tropical Storm Fay re-emerges as a tropical depression with a sustained wind of 35 mph amidst a unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño. (Sun Sentinel)

Health and environment

  • 2026–2027 El Niño event
    • The Atacama Desert in Chile reports blossoms of flowers amidst the ongoing El Nino event in the Pacific. (Phys.org)

International relations

  • Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly
    • Sudanese civil war
      • Africa–United States relations
        • The United States and African Union hold the first joint Quad-Quintet talks at the United Nations General Assembly sidelines in a effort to end the ongoing civil war in Sudan. (Sudan Tribune)
    • Belarus–Poland relations
      • Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski and Belarusian Foreign Minister Maxim Ryzhenkov meet at the United Nations General Assembly, making it the first meeting between Poland and Belarus in a decade. (UA News) (Notes from Poland)
  • Azerbaijan–France relations
    • Azerbaijani president Ilham Aliyev pardons a French national who served a 10-year prison sentence for espionage, and orders his release as one of 20 pardoned prisoners. (BBC News)
  • Cross-strait relations
    • Taiwan's coast guard increases patrol capacity around the disputed Pratas Island in the South China Sea by stationing a new 100-tonne patrol boat and regularly deploying larger vessels, citing increased China Coast Guard activity near the Taiwan-controlled outpost. (Reuters)
  • North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war, South Korea–Ukraine relations
    • Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Ukraine transferred two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea after capturing them in Kursk Oblast, Russia, in January 2025. (UPI)

Law and crime

  • Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases
    • A court in New York, United States, sentences former film producer Harvey Weinstein to 15 years in prison for committing a criminal sexual act against former production assistant Miriam Haley. (BBC News)
  • Mexican drug war, missing persons in Mexico
    • Congresswoman Margarita López Pérez reports that, since 2021, Searching Mothers have found around 1,600 milk teeth, among other skeletal remains, in a mass grave in Zacapu, Michoacán. The state prosecutor's office denies having reports on the case. (Guillermo Ortega)
  • War crimes in the Myanmar civil war
    • Human Rights Watch reports that women held as political prisoners in Myanmar face torture, sexual violence, and inadequate medical care. The group says more than 6,600 women and 640 children are among over 30,000 political prisoners detained since 2021. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Israeli legislative election
    • The Central Elections Committee votes to disqualify Ra'am and all parties on the Joint List from running, alleging they promoted terrorism against Israel. Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh and MK Ofer Cassif are also specifically barred from running. (Times of Israel)
  • 2026 Moroccan general election
    • Moroccans vote to elect all 395 members of the House of Representatives. (AP)
  • Second impeachment of Sara Duterte
    • The Philippine Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, rules that only senator-judges able to participate count toward the conviction threshold in vice president Sara Duterte's trial, reducing the required votes from 16 to 14. (Reuters)
  • The United Kingdom establishes a National Centre for Information Defence to detect and counter foreign disinformation, including AI-generated content. Prime Minister Andy Burnham says the centre will address disinformation attacks to states such as Russia. (AFP via France 24)

Science and technology

  • 2026 OpenAI infiltration of Medicare
    • Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese says that an OpenAI-deployed agent accessed public and restricted files on a Medicare database during testing in June. OpenAI notified the government in September, while investigations continue into the breach. (AFP via France 24) (The Guardian)
  • Croatia joins the U.S.-led Artemis Accords, becoming the 74th country to do so. (Croatia Week)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • North Korea at the 2026 Asian Games, Weightlifting at the 2026 Asian Games
      • North Korean weightlifter Ri Song Gum wins gold in the women's 49kg category at the 2026 Asian Games while setting three world records: 94kg in the snatch, 121kg in the clean and jerk, and 215kg overall. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - September 29, 2026
item.description:
September 29, 2026 (2026-09-29) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Gaza war
    • Israeli settler violence, Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
      • More than 100 Israeli settlers attack the Palestinian village of Jalud in the occupied West Bank, burning two homes and injuring three Israeli security personnel while preventing a displaced Palestinian family from returning home. (AFP via The Manila Times)
    • An Israeli airstrike kills Izz al-Din al-Beik, the head of Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades in the northern Gaza Strip. (Reuters)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Piracy off the coast of Somalia, Anti-piracy measures, Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
      • The Puntland Maritime Police Force successfully frees another hijacked oil tanker, the MT Honour ​25, following an ongoing week-long counter-piracy operation near Bayla, Karkaar, Puntland, after it was seized by Somali pirates on 21 April ​around 30 nautical miles off Puntland's coast with 17 crew members on board. (Reuters) (Somali Guardian)
      • Five crew members aboard the MT Honour 25 are killed and four more injured by the pirates before the rescue. The victims are three citizens of Pakistan and one each from India and Myanmar. It is the first time in over a decade that people are killed by the pirates. (Al Jazeera)

Arts and culture

  • The coronation ceremony for Nyabongo I of Uganda's Tooro Kingdom is held, formally making him king. (Reuters)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • The Reserve Bank of Australia raises its cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.60%, the highest level since 2011, citing persistently high inflation above its 2–3% target range. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)
  • Julius Baer Group controversies
    • The Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) concludes its investigation into the Julius Baer Group, finding serious risk-management and anti–money laundering failures. FINMA orders additional capital requirements, compliance reporting through 2032, and the confiscation of about CHF10 million (US$12 million) in profits. (AFP via France 24)

Disasters and accidents

  • A vehicle crashes through a fence and plunges into the River Wear in Sunderland, Tyne and Wear, England, killing three teenagers. The driver of the vehicle, also a teenager, is later arrested by Northumbria Police. (Sky News)

Health and environment

  • The Japan Meteorological Agency reports rainfall in Tokyo for 34 consecutive days through today, the longest streak since records began in 1886 and one day longer than the previous record set in 2019. (AFP via France 24) (Bloomberg)
  • The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issues two recalls for more than 25,000 bottles of chlorthalidone, a diuretic antihypertensive drug, created by Indian-based Inventia Healthcare Limited, due to faulty dissolution times in the human body. (USA Today)

International relations

  • North Korea–South Korea relations
    • Korean conflict
      • South Korean defense minister Kang Shin-chul says that land mines planted by North Korea likely caused two explosions last week that injured three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone south of the military demarcation line, potentially violating the armistice. (AFP via RFI)
  • Haitian crisis
    • The United Nations Security Council extends the mandate of the Gang Suppression Force in Haiti by six months, allowing the multinational force to continue supporting Haitian security forces against armed gangs. (AFP via RFI)
  • Malaysia–Myanmar relations, Myanmar civil war
    • Malaysia begins repatriating about 1,500 Burmese nationals from immigration detention centres under the first phase of a programme covering 5,000 people. (AFP via RTL Today)

Law and crime

  • Myanmar civil war
    • Twenty-one people are arrested in Myanmar for allegedly donating to the in-exile National Unity Government-linked People's Revolution Supply Family fundraising platform as the government identifies more than 2,700 alleged contributors. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Staškov school stabbing
    • A teacher is killed and a student and another teacher are wounded in a mass stabbing at a secondary school in Staškov, Slovakia. The perpetrator, a fellow student, is arrested. (Euronews)
  • Crime in Mexico
    • The Supreme Court of Mexico invalidates the state of Chihuahua's authority to annul elections due to interference by organized crime and instructs the local legislature to instead include the annulment of elections due to foreign interference. (El Sol de México)
  • Seventeen people are arrested during a security operation involving 800 police officers against a "suspected organised crime group" in five cities in the United Kingdom, including London. A police officer is stabbed and wounded during one of the raids. (Sky News)
  • The Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park in Valencia, California, U.S., announces that the X2 roller coaster will close permanently after several lawsuits alleged that over 100 riders sustained brain injuries while riding the attraction. (BBC)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Moroccan general election
    • King Mohammed VI appoints Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the first female prime minister of Morocco after her victory in the general elections on 23 September. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • Badminton at the 2026 Asian Games, South Korea at the 2026 Asian Games
      • In badminton, South Korea's An Se-young wins the women's singles gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games, becoming the first woman to win two singles titles and the first to defend the title, defeating Japan's Akane Yamaguchi 21–17, 21–9. (AFP via RFI)
  • Manchester City F.C. financial breaches scandal
    • In association football, an independent Premier League commission finds Manchester City guilty of almost all 115-plus financial charges, including inflating revenue by more than £900 million (US$1.19 billion) and failing to cooperate with the investigation. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - September 22, 2026
item.description:
September 22, 2026 (2026-09-22) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Yemeni civil war
    • Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • The Houthi-affiliated Saba News Agency reports that Saudi airstrikes on the Houthi-held city of Mokha, Yemen, have killed six civilians. (AFP via CNA)
  • Colombian conflict
    • Colombian president Abelardo de la Espriella deploys troops to Santa Marta, Magdalena Department, after members of the Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada (ACSN) attack businesses and burn vehicles following a security operation that killed 13 ACSN members, including a senior commander. (AFP)

Arts and culture

  • Silver Roman coins dating back to the 2nd century are discovered by an amateur archaeologist in Germany. The coins are placed on display at the Rheinisches Landesmuseum Bonn museum in Bonn. (The Guardian)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Pacific hurricane season
    • The National Hurricane Center reports that Hurricane Polo has strengthened into a category 5 Pacific hurricane. (The Independent)
  • 2026 Pacific typhoon season
    • Typhoon Dujuan kills at least four people and injures 22 others in Japan, while six remain missing after landslides. More than 45,000 households in Chiba Prefecture lose power, and over 460 homes are damaged. (AFP via Taipei Times)
  • Moldova's parliament approves a 60-day state of emergency in the energy and water sectors as low levels in the Dniester and Prut rivers threaten water supplies and global conflicts raise energy costs. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • The Atlantic hurricane season breaks a 112-year record without a hurricane, due to a strong El Niño event in the Pacific. (AccuWeather)
  • Tunisia's meteorological service reports that summer 2026 is the country's hottest since records began in 1950, with average temperatures 2.9 °C (5.2 °F) above the previous record and repeated heat waves contributing to water shortages and power cuts. (AFP)

International relations

  • Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
        • Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff hold three hours of Qatar-mediated talks at the UN General Assembly in New York City, the first contact between the countries since U.S. vice president JD Vance met an Iranian delegation in Switzerland in June. (The Guardian)
    • Sudan–United States relations
      • Diplomatic sources and the United Nations say that the United States refused to issue Sudanese military chief and de facto leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan a visa to attend the UN General Assembly. Sudan asks the UN to intervene. (AFP)
    • United States–Venezuela relations
      • United States president Donald Trump and Venezuelan interim president Delcy Rodríguez meet on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, marking the first in-person meeting between the countries' leaders following the 2026 U.S. intervention in Venezuela and capture of Nicolás Maduro. (AFP via France 24)
  • Afghanistan–Turkmenistan relations
    • Afghanistan and Turkmenistan agree to establish a joint commission on road transport and to facilitate transit between the two bordering countries. (Trend News Agency)
  • Belgium–Rwanda relations
    • Belgium and Rwanda restore diplomatic relations 18 months after severing ties over the Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict. The countries plan to reopen their embassies following months of meetings facilitated in part by Qatar. (Reuters)
  • Greenland crisis
    • Denmark, Greenland, and the United States sign an agreement expanding U.S. military access to Greenland, permitting new defence areas and a missile defence system while reaffirming Greenland's self-determination and amending the 1951 defence agreement. (DW) (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Crime in South Africa
    • Eleven people are killed, including a pregnant woman, and three others are injured after three men open fire at a gathering inside a house in KwaMakhutha township, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. (BBC News)
    • Three men are killed in a shooting in Gugulethu, Cape Flats, South Africa. Police are investigating it as a triple homicide. (Cape Town ETC)
  • 2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings
    • Sri Lanka's High Court convicts 15 men involved in the Easter bombings in 2019. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 Turgutlu school shooting
    • Eleven people are wounded in a mass shooting at a high school in Turgutlu, Turkey. The perpetrator is arrested. (Al Jazeera)
  • Human trafficking in Papua New Guinea
    • Papua New Guinea police rescue 39 Indonesians allegedly trafficked through false job offers and held in Port Moresby. Officers arrest four Chinese nationals and investigate possible links to a wider transnational trafficking network. (AFP via The Straits Times)
  • Three lawsuits are filed against the Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park in Valencia, California, U.S., after 100 riders suffered brain injuries after riding the X2 roller coaster. (The Guardian) (CBS Los Angeles)
  • Cybercrime group ShinyHunters says it has breached the website of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and stolen personal data on current and former employees, including addresses and Social Security numbers. The FBI investigates the claim. (Reuters)
  • At least three people are killed in an after-curfew ambush in Mangu, Plateau State, Nigeria. (Daily Trust)

Science and technology

  • Hundreds of flights are delayed at five primary airports across northeastern United States, namely Newark Liberty, Teterboro, Philadelphia, LaGuardia, and JFK, due to technological issues after a construction crew accidentally severed numerous cables, including fiber-optic ones used for communication with air traffic control. (BBC News) (CNN)

item.title: Current Events - September 24, 2026
item.description:
September 24, 2026 (2026-09-24) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war, France–Saudi Arabia relations
      • Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
        • 2026 Yemen offensives
          • France announces that it will deploy its soldiers and air defense systems to Yanbu, Saudi Arabia, to support the Saudi military against the Houthis. (Reuters)
    • Gaza war
      • The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet say that they have killed Hamas's chief financial officer in the Khan Younis area of the Gaza Strip. (Israel National News) (The Yeshiva World)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • Fano fighters launch several attacks in the Amhara Region. Shootouts with the Ethiopian National Defense Force are ongoing, causing several casualties, while a colonel is captured. (Daily News Egypt)
  • 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
    • Pakistan's military launches ten air strikes on Afghan military sites, killing four people. (AP)

Arts and culture

  • The beatification ceremony for the late American Catholic prelate and Rochester Archbishop Fulton J. Sheen is held at The Dome at America's Center in St. Louis, Missouri, United States. (Bastille Post) (Vatican News)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
      • The European Commission reports that the average diesel price across the European Union reaches a record €2.23 (US$2.54) per litre, up from €2.16 ($2.46) the previous week. Nineteen member states record new highs. (AFP via Bangkok Post)
    • Economic D-Day, United States sanctions against Iran
      • The Emirati General Civil Aviation Authority announces the suspension of all flights between Iran and the United Arab Emirates amidst new U.S. sanctions until further notice. (Gulf News)
  • Economic impact of the Gaza war
    • UN Trade and Development reports that Gaza is experiencing the most severe economic crisis on record, with 92% of economic establishments damaged or destroyed, daily per capita GDP at US$0.58, and unemployment exceeding 90% among working-age residents. (AFP)

Disasters and accidents

  • At least nine people are killed and many others are injured after a sleeper bus catches fire on the Yamuna Expressway in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India. (Deccan Herald) (DW)
  • Twelve Kazakh military personnel are killed, three are rescued and two are missing after being swept into the Caspian Sea during a naval training exercise in the Mangystau Region. (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • Hungary's food chain safety office confirms the European Union's first detection of the invasive spotted lanternfly in Bács-Kiskun County. (AFP via France 24)

Law and crime

  • Chromebook procurement scandal
    • A court in Jakarta, Indonesia, reduces former education minister and Gojek co-founder Nadiem Makarim's prison sentence from 10 to nine years for corruption involving Chromebook procurement, while lowering restitution from Rp809 billion (US$45 million) to Rp548 billion ($30 million). (Reuters)
  • Croatia–Germany relations, Nord Stream pipelines sabotage
    • A Croatian court approves Ukrainian national Volodymyr Zhuravlov's extradition to Germany over his alleged involvement in sabotaging the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 pipelines in 2022. (AP)
  • Donald Trump's conflict with the news media
    • American news outlets CNN, MS NOW, and Politico regain access to the White House after U.S. federal judge Timothy J. Kelly temporarily blocked the ban by President Donald Trump, ruling that the outlets are likely to show that their press passes were revoked without adequate due process. (BBC News)
  • Mary Jane Veloso drug smuggling case
    • Philippine president Bongbong Marcos grants an absolute pardon to Mary Jane Veloso, a former overseas worker in Indonesia who was arrested for drug trafficking and sentenced to death in 2010, but was later granted a reprieve and extradited back to the Philippines. (Reuters) (Philippine Daily Inquirer)
  • Belarusian president Alexander Lukashenko says that he has pardoned 15 political prisoners. (Reuters)
  • A priest is killed and four other people are injured in a mass stabbing by a Ukrainian national at a Benedictine abbey in Jarosław, Podkarpackie Voivodeship, Poland. (AP) (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Moroccan general election
    • Morocco's Authenticity and Modernity Party, led by Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, wins the most seats in yesterday's parliamentary election, taking 97 of 395 seats, followed by the ruling National Rally of Independents with 66 and the Istiqlal Party with 65, according to preliminary official results. (Reuters)
  • Hijab and burqa controversies in Europe, Islam in Italy
    • Italy's government approves a decree capping foreign students with limited Italian proficiency at 30% per classroom and banning burqas and niqabs in schools. The measure takes effect immediately but requires parliamentary approval within 60 days. (AP)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • Japan at the 2026 Asian Games, Swimming at the 2026 Asian Games
      • In swimming, Japan's Shin Ohashi wins gold in the men's 200-metre breaststroke at the 2026 Asian Games in 2:04.83, breaking China's Qin Haiyang's 2023 world record of 2:05.48 by 0.65 seconds. (AFP)
  • 2026 Major League Baseball season
    • In baseball, the Major League Baseball's Chicago White Sox clinches the upcoming playoffs for the first time since 2021, following three-straight 100-loss seasons. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - October 01, 2026
item.description:
October 1, 2026 (2026-10-01) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Iraqi conflict
    • Withdrawal of United States troops from Iraq
      • Ahmad al-Hamidawi, leader of Kata'ib Hezbollah, announces that the group will suspend military activities in Iraq following the withdrawal of U.S. troops, with the exception of targeting hostile aircraft violating the country's airspace. (Middle East Eye)
  • Israeli–Palestinian conflict
    • Israeli settler violence, Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war
      • Israeli settlers shoot and kill a Palestinian man at his home in Yasuf, West Bank, and injure another. (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Aviation shootdowns and accidents during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Russian Su-35 fighter jet shoots down a Russian Mi-8 helicopter over Voronezh Oblast, Russia, in a friendly fire incident. All three crew members are killed. (Kyiv Independent)
  • Sudanese civil war, Kordofan campaign
    • War crimes in the Sudanese civil war
      • A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces on a dormitory at the University of Kordofan in El Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, kills five people. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • Explosions caused by suspected drone strikes are reported in Ethiopia's capital of Addis Abeba, including one near the Ethiopian National Defense Force' headquarters. (BBC News)
  • 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
    • Pakistan launches airstrikes in Afghanistan, claiming the killing of 22 Taliban fighters at two locations, while the Government of Afghanistan reports that nine women and children are killed in Kunar Province and Helmand Province by Pakistan airstrikes. (Al Jazeera)

Disasters and accidents

  • A medical helicopter transporting a patient crashes off the coast of Santa Catalina Island in Los Angeles County, California, United States, killing two people, injuring two others, and leaving one missing. (AP)

International relations

  • Ethiopian civil conflict, TPLF insurgency in Ethiopia
    • Eritrea–Ethiopia relations
      • Ethiopia closes its embassy in Eritrea and announces the expulsion of ten Eritrean diplomats from the country, after accusing its neighbour of financing the Tigray People's Liberation Front. (AP)
      • Eritrea's foreign ministry announces that the country will cut off diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in response. (AFP via Al Arabiya) (Reuters)
    • Egypt–Ethiopia relations
      • A diplomat from Egypt is told to leave Ethiopia within 48 hours after being declared as persona non grata. (Reuters)
  • The European Commission stops payments with immediate effect to Sierra Leone, which would have been €18 million for 2026, after the nation refused to cooperate with the extradition of drugs trafficker Jos Leijdekkers. (Het Parool)

Law and crime

  • Censorship in Egypt, Human rights in Egypt
    • Egyptian police are arresting six journalists from a fact-checking and investigative media outlet, accusing them of spreading misinformation on behalf of the banned Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt. (Reuters)
  • 2026 RAF Fairford arrests
    • British counter-terrorism police arrest a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national in Westminster, London, England, on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts linked to the RAF Fairford investigation. Officers also search two properties in the area. (CNN)
  • Sentencing Act 2026
    • Hundreds of prisoners begin leaving prison in England and Wales under an early release scheme by the British government to avoid overcapacity in prisons. More than 4,500 "low-risk" prisoners are expected to be released in the coming weeks. (BBC News) (Firstpost)
  • Former Malawian military chief Paul Valentino Phiri is arrested by Malawi's anti-corruption agency for allegedly trafficking weapons to Sudan during his tenure in June and July 2025. (Al-Monitor)
  • Two 18-year-old former students attack a secondary school in Torreón, Coahuila, Mexico, with knives and pyrotechnic devices, killing the vice-principal and injuring three people. Police arrest both suspects. (AFP via RNZ)

Politics and elections

  • Immigration to Japan
    • Japan tightens permanent residency requirements for foreign nationals, introducing above-average income and basic Japanese-language standards while raising application fees twentyfold as part of broader changes to immigration policy. (AFP)
  • Gerardo Giovagnoli and William Casali are sworn in as the new Captains Regent of San Marino, succeeding Alice Mina and Vladimiro Selva. (San Marino RTV)
  • Ousted Sudanese leader Omar al-Bashir is sent to a military hospital in Khartoum, Sudan, for medical treatment. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • SpaceX Crew-13
    • The SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station launches, carrying two NASA astronauts, one Roscosmos cosmonaut, and one Canadian Space Agency astronaut, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, United States. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - September 27, 2026
item.description:
September 27, 2026 (2026-09-27) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Yemeni civil war
    • Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
      • 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Saudi Arabia's air force carries out an airstrike at a market in Taiz, Yemen, killing seven people and wounding 40 more. (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Kyiv strikes, Odesa strikes, Zaporizhzhia strikes
      • Russian and Ukrainian forces exchange strikes that kill at least eight people in Ukraine and one in Russia, hitting Kyiv and its outskirts, the Kharkiv and Odesa Oblasts, Sumy, and Russian-occupied Enerhodar, all in Ukraine, as well as Russia's Belgorod Oblast. (AP)
    • Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
      • Russian strikes hit Kyivstar's headquarters and multiple data centres in Kyiv, including a facility struck twice that injures two children and an adult. Russia also says it targeted a Vodafone Ukraine data centre. (India Today)
  • 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
    • Islamic State–Taliban conflict
      • The Afghan military kill 28 fighters allegedly linked to the Islamic State in Nuristan Province. The Minister of Defense reports that the gunmen entered from Pakistan. (Al Jazeera)
  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • A drone strikes Tigrai Television's headquarters in Mekelle, Tigray Region, Ethiopia, forcing the station off air, while Tigray People's Liberation Front forces capture Erebti, Afar Region, and advance toward Afdera. (AFP via France 24)

Business and economy

  • Turkish economic crisis
    • Former Turkish family minister Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya resigns from her positions in the ruling Justice and Development Party amid scrutiny over alleged links to an investment-fund scandal that prompted the Capital Markets Board to liquidate 131 funds and led to 51 arrests. (AFP) (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • A bus carrying Filipino tourists veers off a highway near Munich, Germany, killing two people and wounding 25 more. (AP) (Demócrata)

Health and environment

  • Healthcare in Ireland
    • The Irish public healthcare system announces they will limit influenza vaccines to people aged 65 and above due to a shortage across the country. (RTÉ)

International relations

  • China–United States relations
    • Panda diplomacy
      • Two giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, arrive at Zoo Atlanta in Georgia, U.S., as part of an agreement signed between China and the U.S. during Chinese leader Xi Jinping's state visit last week. (AFP via Dawn) (AP)

Law and crime

  • 2026 RAF Fairford arrests
    • Five men are arrested in relation to a 'major incident' at the RAF Fairford air base in England. They are arrested on suspicion of committing offences that violate the Explosives Act 1875 and preparation of a terrorist act. (CNN) (The Guardian)
  • Crime in South Africa
    • Ten people are killed and 11 others are injured in a mass shooting at a store in Lwandle, City of Cape Town, South Africa. Police search for the perpetrators. A business dispute is suspected to be the main motive. (Euronews)
  • Kidnapping in Nigeria
    • It is reported that armed gangs have kidnapped at least 47 farmers in Niger State, Nigeria, yesterday and 40 women in Zamfara State on today. Separately, Abia State police announce on that they have discovered 28 human skulls and bones after raiding camps suspected to be owned by criminal gangs, with police speculating they may belong to kidnapped victims. (Al Jazeera)
  • Three people are killed and four more injured in a mass shooting after an altercation at a strip club in Detroit, Michigan, United States. (Al Jazeera)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 French Senate election
    • The National Rally clears the 10-seat threshold in the Senate of France, allowing the party to meet qualifications to form a far-right parliamentary group. (The Guardian) (RFI)
  • 2026 São Toméan parliamentary election
    • São Toméans vote to elect 55 members of the National Assembly. (AFP via Macau Business)
  • 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
    • Serbian president Aleksandar Vučić resigns in order to run for prime minister in the upcoming parliamentary election. Speaker of the National Assembly Ana Brnabić becomes acting president. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Swiss referendums
    • Swiss voters reject an initiative that proposed to enshrine a stricter form of Swiss neutrality, which would have prevented Switzerland from imposing economic sanctions and cooperating with NATO. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Berlin Marathon
    • The Berlin Marathon is held in Germany, with Guye Adola and Tigst Assefa winning their respective marathon races although Assefa sustained cramps prior to the finish line. (AP) (BBC News)
  • 2026 Billie Jean King Cup
    • In tennis, the Czech Republic wins its 12th Billie Jean King Cup title and first since 2018 after defeating Ukraine 2–0 in the final in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. (AFP)
  • 2026 UCI Road World Championships
    • In cycling, Brandon McNulty of the United States wins the men's road race world title in Montreal, Canada, becoming the first American champion in 33 years after finishing 13 seconds ahead of Australia's Michael Matthews. (AFP)

item.title: Current Events - September 20, 2026
item.description:
September 20, 2026 (2026-09-20) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
        • Qatar as a mediator in conflict
          • Qatar's foreign ministry says that they are working to resume ceasefire negotiations between Iran and the United States. (Middle East Eye)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Ukrainian forces launch a massive drone attack on Moscow Oblast, Russia, with more than 1,600 long-range drones launched from Ukraine. At least two people are killed with hundreds more evacuated while Moscow Refinery is on fire following several direct hits. (Al Jazeera)
      • Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirms he ordered the attack on Moscow in response to Russian forces targeting civilians in Ukrainian cities, saying that FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles and ballistic missiles were also used in the attack. (L'Unione Sarda)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • The Statistical Center of Iran reports that the country's gross domestic product contracted 10.1% year-on-year from late March to late June, during the war, amid longstanding sanctions and currency depreciation. (AFP via The Straits Times)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • The National Hurricane Center reports that Tropical Depression Six strengthened into Tropical Storm Fay amidst an unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño, becoming the sixth named storm of the season. (AccuWeather) (WFLA-TV)
  • Eight people are killed and another is injured in a fire at a textile factory in Guangdong Province, China. (Reuters)
  • Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured after the explosion of a gas cylinder in Ashulia, Bangladesh. (Xinhua)
  • Six people are killed when a bus plunges about fifteen meters into a ravine in Cruzeiro, Brazil. (G1 in Portuguese)(Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Democratic Republic of the Congo launches vaccinations for frontline workers amdist the Ebola outbreak in the country. (Africanews)

International relations

  • France–Iran relations
    • Iranian authorities close down a French language centre affiliated with the French embassy in Tehran under a judicial order. Prosecutors say it operated without a licence and conducted activities against Iranian culture and national security. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Assassination of Jovenel Moïse, Haiti–United States relations
    • Haiti sends 18 suspects in the July 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moïse to the United States to face federal charges related to the killing. (Reuters)
  • Pakistani police arrest businesswoman Aleema Khan, sister of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, at her home in Lahore, Punjab, one week before his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party's planned protest march. Police and the government do not state a reason for the arrest. (Reuters)
  • Four unauthorized miners are killed in a shooting targeting a vehicle by unidentified gunmen in Barkin Ladi, Plateau State, Nigeria. (Daily Post Nigeria)
  • Three people are killed and another is injured in a mass shooting at a shack in an informal settlement in Philippi, Cape Flats, South Africa. (SABC)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Mecklenburg-Vorpommern state election, 2026 Berlin state election
    • State elections are held in Germany for the Landtag of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and the Berlin House of Representatives, with an expected decline for the Chancellor Friedrich Merz's party, the CDU. (BBC News)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • Japan at the 2026 Asian Games, Triathlon at the 2026 Asian Games
      • Japanese triathlete Takumi Hojo wins the first gold medal of the 2026 Asian Games. (AFP)
  • 2026 UCI Road World Championships
    • In cycling, Belgian rider Remco Evenepoel becomes the first man to win four consecutive Road World Championship titles in the individual time trial event and equals Fabian Cancellara and Tony Martin's joint record for the most titles. Swiss rider Marlen Reusser wins the women's time trial event. (AFP via The Guardian)

item.title: Current Events - September 26, 2026
item.description:
September 26, 2026 (2026-09-26) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
    • A Pakistani Taliban suicide bomber self-detonates at a police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing twelve people and wounding 30 more. (Al Jazeera) (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Bangkok floods
    • In Thailand, Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt declares a flood disaster across the city as severe flooding kills at least two people and affects more than 84,000 nationwide. (AFP via France 24) (AP)
  • September 2026 nor'easter
    • A nor'easter is reported along the East Coast of the United States, forcing the cancellation of 400 flights and leaving more than 68,000 homes without power. One person is killed in New York City, New York. (Reuters) (WABC-TV)
  • Seven sailors are injured and 25 are rescued after a fire breaks out aboard the Russian fishing vessel Triumf off the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Far East. (Reuters)

International relations

  • Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly
    • Germany–Russia relations
      • German foreign minister Johann Wadephul and Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov hold talks during the United Nations General Assembly, the first talks between Germany and Russia since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Crime in South Africa
    • Seventeen people are killed and 15 more are injured in a mass shooting carried out by eight gunmen at the KwaNoxolo tavern in Bekkersdal, Westonaria near Carletonville, Gauteng, South Africa. Police launch a manhunt for the gunmen. (The Citizen) (CNN)
    • The body of a murdered woman is found in Ekurhuleni, South Africa. She is the tenth woman found killed in the city in the last three months. Police says that it can not rule out the possibility that the killings are carried out by a serial killer. (BBC News)

Politics and elections

  • India's Election Commission orders a review of its voter-roll software after concerns arise over changes that excluded millions of voters. A committee will examine whether the software complied with election laws and rules. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 AFL Grand Final
    • In Australian rules football, the Brisbane Lions defeat the Fremantle Dockers to win the 2026 Australian Football League season by seven points, winning their third consecutive premiership and sixth overall. (AFL) (The Guardian)
  • 2026 Billie Jean King Cup finals
    • In tennis, Ukraine reaches its first Billie Jean King Cup final after defeating defending champion Italy 2–0 in the semifinals, with Elina Svitolina securing the decisive victory over Jasmine Paolini. (AFP) (AP)
  • 2026 UCI Road World Championships
    • In cycling, the Netherlands' Demi Vollering wins the women's road race world title in Montreal, Canada, defeating Poland's Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney in the final sprint, while Italy's Elisa Longo Borghini takes bronze. (AFP)
  • Bids for the 2036 Summer Olympics
    • Germany's Olympic committee selects Munich as its candidate to host the Summer Olympics and Paralympics in 2036, 2040, or 2044. (AP)

item.title: Current Events - September 19, 2026
item.description:
September 19, 2026 (2026-09-19) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
        • Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaee says that Iran has set seven conditions for resuming ceasefire negotiations with the United States. (Iran International)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • United States Central Command commander Brad Cooper says that oil, cargo, and liquefied natural gas shipments in the Strait of Hormuz have hit a six-month high. (Bloomberg) (Middle East Eye)
    • Gaza war
      • Israeli airstrikes kill at least three Palestinians in Gaza, including the eldest son of the Gaza Health Ministry director-general. Israel says it targeted militants, while medics report additional deaths in Sheikh Radwan and Shuja'iyya. (Reuters)
  • Operation Southern Spear
    • United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear
      • The U.S. military strikes a vessel in the Caribbean Sea, killing four people whom the Southern Command says were involved in drug trafficking. (Reuters)
  • Islamic State insurgency in the Philippines
    • A series of clashes, involving combined police and military forces and remaining wanted members of the Dawlah Islamiya and the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters, erupts in Tugunan, Special Geographic Area of the Bangsamoro, Philippines. Seven members from both groups are killed. (The Philippine Star)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Atlantic hurricane season
    • Tropical Depression Six forms in the Atlantic Ocean near the Azores amidst an unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season caused by El Niño. (Fox Weather) (WTSP)
  • 2026 Indonesia wildfires, Indonesia–Malaysia relations
    • Indonesia accepts Malaysian assistance to combat wildfires in Kalimantan, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters, and 52 personnel, as the fires cause transboundary haze affecting Southeast Asia. (AFP via France 24)

International relations

  • Eritrea–United States relations
    • The U.S. treasury department lifts the sanctions against Eritrea's ruling party previously imposed by former U.S. president Joe Biden's administration. (AP)
  • 2026 United Nations Secretary-General selection
    • Chilean Michelle Bachelet announces that she is withdrawing from the race to become UN Secretary-General after losing support, and that in the latest informal poll, Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan is reported in the lead. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Domestic violence in South Africa, Sexual violence in South Africa
    • South Africans hold memorial runs and protests after police find the bodies of nine women in Ekurhuleni, Gauteng, over two months. Police investigate possible links between the killings, which renew public concern over violence against women. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Russian legislative election
    • Russian election commission chairperson Ella Pamfilova reports cyberattacks targeting Russia's online voting system during the second day of the parliamentary election and says they are repelled. The Minkomsvyaz separately reports thwarting a sabotage attempt on Far Eastern communication lines. (ABC News Australia)
  • 2026 South Ossetian presidential election
    • Marat Kambolov is declared the winner of the presidential elections in the partially recognized South Ossetia. (Reuters)
  • Donald Trump's conflict with the news media
    • United States president Donald Trump's executive office denies journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico access to the White House and confiscates or disables their press passes, citing their coverage of his administration. (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • The 20th Asian Games are opened by Emperor Naruhito in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. (Reuters)
  • 2026 WNBA season
    • In women's basketball, Atlanta Dream player Angel Reese becomes the first player in Women's National Basketball Association history to reach 500 rebounds in a single season. (Bleacher Report)
  • 2026 World Rugby Pacific Nations Cup
    • In rugby union, hosts Japan win their fourth Pacific Nations Cup title after defeating the defending champions Fiji 20–15 in the final at Chichibunomiya Stadium in Tokyo. (AFP via RFI)

item.title: Current Events - September 28, 2026
item.description:
September 28, 2026 (2026-09-28) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Kyiv strikes, Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure
      • At least three people are killed and 24 others, including the former secretary of the National Security and Defence Council, Volodymyr Horbulin, are injured by Russian drone strikes on the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine building, a health clinic, and a residential building in Kyiv, Ukraine. (The Guardian) (Ukrainska Pravda)
    • Polish military jets are scrambled in response to Russian airstrikes on Ukraine. Individuals in Lublin Voivodeship, Poland, are briefly urged to seek shelter before an alert is lifted. (Reuters)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Constitutional crisis in Somalia, Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud
      • At least 23 people are killed and others are injured as heavy clashes breaks out across the South West State of Somalia, as forces loyal to former president Abdiaziz Laftagareen launch a major armed assault on troops of Aden Madobe and Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. The assault starts with gunfire, explosive drones and a suicide vehicle bomb, spreading through the regional capital Baidoa. (Garowe Online) (Horseed Media) (Bluewin)
  • Myanmar civil war
    • Rakhine offensive
      • At least 50 people are killed and 58 others are injured in a Tatmadaw airstrike on a market area in Kyauktaw, Rakhine State, Myanmar. The strike targeted the Arakan Army, which controls Kyauktaw. (AFP via France 24)
  • Haitian crisis
    • Gang members kill at least eleven civilians in Gros Morne, Grand'Anse, Haiti, after exchanging fire with a Gang Suppression Force patrol, which kills three attackers before the remaining gunmen flee. (Demócrata)

Business and economy

  • Russian president Vladimir Putin places German retailer Metro AG's Russian assets under temporary administration, removing Metro's operational control amid broader Russian restrictions on businesses from countries it classifies as unfriendly. (AP)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Bangkok floods
    • Flooding and landslides kill at least eight people each in Myanmar and Thailand, while 20 to 30 people remain missing in Tanintharyi Region and more than 1.7 million people across Bangkok and 27 Thai provinces are affected. (AFP via France 24)
  • 2026 Pacific hurricane season
    • Hurricane Polo causes flooding, power outages, coastal flooding, and evacuations in Baja California Sur, Mexico, as the Category 3 storm approaches the Pacific coast, becoming the first Pacific hurricane of the 2026 season to make landfall. (AFP)
  • Eighty-one people in Uttar Pradesh, India, and 21 more in Nepal are killed during heavy floods and landslides in the past three days. (Euronews)
  • An avalanche kills four climbers and leaves 12 others missing at the base camp of the Himalayan mountain Nemjung in Manang District, Nepal, as heavy snowfall hampers rescue operations. (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • Sudanese cholera epidemic
    • United Nations Secretary-General spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric reports a sharp drop in cholera cases in Sudan despite the ongoing civil war in the country following vaccinations and extensive efforts to treat the disease. (Sudan Tribune)
  • The government of Delhi, India, announces a six-week construction ban from December 10 to January 20, along with traffic restrictions, staggered office hours, and higher parking fees, as part of measures to reduce winter air pollution. (AFP via Gulf Times)

Law and crime

  • Five people are arrested in a police raid against suspected Islamic State members in Skopje, North Macedonia. Guns, knives and the group's flag are recovered. (Vesnik)
  • Dutch police arrest cybersecurity specialist Pepijn van der Stap in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacker group. Van der Stap's employer identifies him as the suspect, while police say he will appear in court in Rotterdam, South Holland. (CBC News)

Science and technology

  • Starship flight 14
    • SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 launches into orbit from Starbase, Texas, United States. The ship is successfully returned to Earth early out of an abundance of caution. (Al Jazeera) (AP)

Sports

  • The United States Senate votes 77–22 to pass the Protect College Sports Act, a bill that will establish federal rules governing name, image, and likeness (NIL) compensation, NCAA eligibility, and athlete transfers in college sports. (ESPN)

item.title: Current Events - September 21, 2026
item.description:
September 21, 2026 (2026-09-21) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict, 2026 Yemen offensives
        • Saudi Arabia–United Kingdom relations
          • British prime minister Andy Burnham says that the United Kingdom will offer Saudi Arabia aerial refueling in its ongoing conflict with the Houthis. (The Hill)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Egypt–Sudan relations, Egypt–United States relations, Sudan–United States relations
      • U.S. senior advisor Massad Boulos says that he has held talks with Sudanese foreign minister Mohieddin Salem and Egyptian foreign minister Badr Abdelatty at the United Nations General Assembly meeting in an effort to end the three-year long civil war. (Arab News) (Sudan Horizon)
    • Darfur campaign
      • The Sudanese military at night launches heavy airstrikes against Rapid Support Forces targets in Nyala, South Darfur. (Sudan Tribune)
    • Kordofan campaign
      • An attack on a gold mining market in North Kordofan by the Rapid Support Forces kills five citizens, including a goldsmith worker. (Sudan Tribune)
    • The United Nations's International Organization for Migration reports that 5 million displaced people have decided to return to Sudan despite the civil war. (Arab News)
  • 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
    • Pakistan's military launches strikes over the Afghanistan–Pakistan border in retaliation for the 2026 Kohat attack. Afghanistan's government and the UNAMA report that a family of three was killed in the strikes, while Pakistan says the strikes killed 28 Pakistani Taliban militants. (Reuters)

Arts and culture

  • Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict
    • The Red Sea International Film Festival in Saudi Arabia is postponed to 2027 due to the ongoing conflict with the Houthis. (Arab News) (Gulf News)

Business and economy

  • Ceer Motors unveils the EXOBOT SUV and sedan in Saudi Arabia, its first electric vehicles in the country. (Electrek)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 California wildfires
    • Two pilots are killed in a helicopter crash while fighting a wildfire in Yosemite National Park, California, United States. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Nepal–Tibet floods
    • The Nepalese government announces that they are discussing resettling victims of flooding from Bhotekoshi Rural Municipality to safe places in the country. (Daily Pioneer)
  • Korean conflict
    • An explosion injures three South Korean military officers during an operation inside the Demilitarized Zone, south of the military demarcation line. The Joint Chiefs of Staff says the cause remains unknown. (AFP via The Peninsula)
  • A helicopter crashes in a mountainous area of Urubici, Santa Catarina, Brazil, killing the five occupants, including singer Rick Sollo. (Metrópoles in Portuguese) (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • New Zealand's critically endangered black robin wins Forest & Bird's Bird of the Year competition with more than 26,000 votes out of about 105,000 votes. (AFP)

International relations

  • International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia–European Union relations
    • European Union ambassadors agree in principle to remove Russian oligarchs Mikhail Fridman and Alisher Usmanov from sanctions imposed over Russia's invasion of Ukraine, while renewing restrictions on about 3,000 other Russian-linked individuals and entities for three years. However, Latvia later blocks the deal. (Billionaires.Africa) (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2023 Vermont shooting of Palestinian students
    • Jason Eaton is found guilty for shooting and critically wounding three Palestinian students in Burlington, Vermont, United States, who wore keffiyehs in solidarity with Palestine in the wake of the beginning of the Gaza war. (The Guardian) (IndyStar)
  • Singapore's Land Transport Authority introduces fines of up to S$500 (US$390) for eating on public buses or placing feet on seats, while severe cleanliness or safety violations can incur penalties of up to S$5,000 (US$3,900). (AFP)

Politics and elections

  • Mexico's Secretariat of Public Education introduces nationwide rules restricting cellphone and tablet use throughout the school day in public primary and secondary schools, effective November 3. High schools set their own limits for educational use. (AFP via The Star)

item.title: Current Events - September 25, 2026
item.description:
September 25, 2026 (2026-09-25) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign
      • The Sudanese Armed Forces announces that they have recaptured Sodri, North Kordofan. (Radio Tamazuj)
      • Two civilians are killed in a drone strike by Rapid Support Forces in El Obeid. (Sudan Tribune)
    • Sudanese refugee crisis
      • The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees reports a sharp increase in refugees fleeing from Sudan to Chad in a effort to escape the civil war and dire conditions, with 400 people a day crossing eastern Chad. (Reuters)
  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iran war ceasefire, 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
      • The Wall Street Journal reports that United States president Donald Trump has rejected Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and halt regional fighting within seven days in exchange for easing U.S. sanctions and releasing Iranian frozen funds. (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Kyiv strikes, Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Russian drone and missile strikes on residential buildings and other civilian sites in Kyiv, Ukraine, kill seven people, including a 14-year-old boy, and injure 46 others. (AFP via News.com.au)
  • Somali Civil War
    • Piracy off the coast of Somalia, Anti-piracy measures
      • The Puntland Maritime Police Force successfully frees the oil tanker Sibu 1 following a multi-day counter-piracy operation near Garacad, Mudug, Puntland, after it was seized by Somali pirates in August. (Idil News) (Reuters)
  • 2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war
    • Pakistan says that its military has killed 13 Afghan security forces during shootouts at the border. Afghanistan's government denies the claim. (Al Jazeera) (AP)

Business and economy

  • Gambling in Brazil
    • Days before the general election, Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva issues a provisional measure banning online betting in Brazil, immediately halting new deposits. Users may withdraw remaining funds until October 5, and Congress must approve the measure within 120 days for it to remain in force. (AFP via France 24) (BBC News)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Kenge Let L-410 crash
    • A military-leased Let L-410 carrying 17 people, including two generals, crashes near Kenge, Kwango, Democratic Republic of the Congo, while on route to Kinshasa, killing all passengers. (AA) (Reuters)
  • Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured when a bus overturns on a road near Iraquara, Bahia, Brazil. (G1)
  • Six people are killed and two others injured during the collapse of a two-storey building in Plaka, Athens, Greece, after an explosion caused by a suspected gas leak. (AFP via France 24) (AP) (BBC News)
  • Two people are killed and 13 more injured in a fire at a residential building in Lucca, Tuscany, Italy. (ANSA)

Health and environment

  • 2023–2026 mpox epidemic
    • A laboratory-confirmed mpox case from a 21-year-old woman is reported in Bunia, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. (Reuters)

International relations

  • China–United States relations
    • China–United States trade war, 2026 state visit by Xi Jinping to the United States
      • China and the United States reach an agreement to cut tariffs on $30 ‌billion of goods and launch a dialogue on artificial intelligence. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2026 political prisoner release in Venezuela
    • Venezuela releases at least 29 detainees whom rights groups classify as political prisoners following a second round of talks between the interim government and opposition, while organizations continue verifying the number and identities of those freed. (AFP via RFI)
  • Mary Jane Veloso drug smuggling case
    • Mary Jane Veloso is released from a prison in Mandaluyong, Philippines, after president Bongbong Marcos's absolute pardon of her was approved yesterday. (Arab News) (Rappler)
  • A court in Paris, France, sentences Loik Le Priol to 26 years in prison and Romain Bouvier to 19 years for murdering former Argentine rugby union player Federico Martín Aramburú in 2022. Le Priol and Bouvier had links to the dissolved far-right group Groupe Union Défense. (AP) (BBC News)
  • Sri Lanka's parliament approves a constitutional amendment extending the terms of senior judges by two years as part of efforts to reduce an estimated 1.1 million-case backlog. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Asian Games
    • China at the 2026 Asian Games, Swimming at the 2026 Asian Games
      • In swimming, China's Zhang Zhanshuo becomes the first athlete to win seven gold medals at a single Asian Games, securing his seventh title in the men's 400-metre freestyle with a Games-record time of 3:41.28. (AFP)
  • In association football, an independent Premier League commission finds Manchester City F.C. guilty of 114 of 115 alleged financial-rule breaches spanning the 2009–10 to 2022–23 seasons. (CNN)

item.title: Current Events - October 02, 2026
item.description:
October 2, 2026 (2026-10-02) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Arrmed conflicts and attacks

  • Ethiopian civil conflict
    • 2026 Ethiopian offensive
      • Ethiopian government forces push Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) rebels out of Afar Region after recapturing the towns of Abala, Erebti and Megale. (AFP via France 24)

Business and economy

  • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
    • The G7 countries announce a plan to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil to combat rising fuel prices caused by the Iran war. (The New York Times)

Law and crime

  • 2026 French fuel protests
    • Mass rioting continues for a third day across France with hundreds reportedly injured and over 500 schools shut, while more than 2,000 people are arrested. (BBC News)
    • French government ministers, including education minister Édouard Geffray, accuse the far-left of inciting the youth-led unrest across the country. Intelligence agencies briefing the government during a crisis meeting on the riots say the radical left La France Insoumise are actively inciting people to join the protests. (AFP via NDTV) (Ynet News)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Spanish housing protests
